messages:
katie: Quick 10m sync at 10 to finalize GA acceptance for Adaptive Batching v1. Need a firm call on SLA slices, docs checklist, oncall plan, monitoring gates, and an early-adopter pricing package. Who's in?

maria: In. Priority for me is clear SLO definitions, the error-budget policy, and a published exceptions list before GA. Lean conservative on initial SLAs.

aj: Runtime data: p95 <= 300ms for short sequences on Dedicated in our tests. Long sequences and embeddings have higher variance. Suggest slice-based SLAs: short (<=512 tokens), long (>512), embeddings as separate product.

thomas: Support-side: runbooks must include timeout handling, fallback to smaller model/quantized variant, steps to toggle quantization profiles, and an escalation flow for model-quality regressions. I'll own runbook edits.

katie: Draft GA acceptance candidates: 
- SLA: p95 latency per slice (short) <= 300ms; availability 99.9% for Hosted/Dedicated.
- Docs: runbook, API notes for batch params, customer FAQ, and an internal ops checklist.
- Monitoring: alert when error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 15m OR p95 latency breach across two 15m windows.
- Pricing: publish reserved tiers + burst policy + an early-adopter 3-month promo.
(These are proposals for discussion.)

aj: Operational constraints: default burst = 2x reserved throughput with documented throttling back to commit. Need explicit doc of per-model memory/seq limits that cause 429s. Also document fallback behavior when KV cache pressure triggers evictions.

maria: If we promise 99.9% SLA we must publish exceptions (e.g., DDOS, region-wide cloud outage, scheduled maintenance) and a clear refunds/credit table. Otherwise CS will get a bunch of refund tickets.

sam: CS request: a customer-facing SLA FAQ and a short sales summary explaining credit triggers and timelines. Need an owner.

thomas: Oncall: propose 30-day intensified burn-in after GA with product-SRE primary, infra backup. I'll own runbook + playbook. Need an SLO owner for the math and the postmortem policy.

katie: Decision proposal: ship GA with the SLA floor above, include a 30-day burn-in where we monitor and reserve the right to adjust SLAs if real traffic patterns break our assumptions. Publish exceptions and owners.

katie: Agreed action items:
1) SLO math, error-budget policy, and exceptions list 0 owner: maria 0 due: Thu EOD
2) Runbook & oncall playbook 0 owner: thomas 0 due: Fri EOD
3) Quota/burst docs + throttling and 429 behavior 0 owner: aj 0 due: Fri EOD
4) Customer-facing SLA FAQ + refund timeline (sales one-pager) 0 owner: sam 0 due: Fri EOD
5) Monitoring alerts & dashboards (p95 by slice, error rate, OOMs, evictions) 0 owner: aj 0 due: Fri EOD
6) Lock GA criteria into release checklist if no objections 0 owner: katie 0 due: next Wed noon

ops-bot: Reminder: tabletop invite created for 10:00 0 link in calendar. :bell:

maria: I'll open a PR with SLO calculations and the exceptions draft this afternoon.

katie: Thanks all. If no major objections by EOD Thursday we'll lock these GA acceptance criteria and proceed with the 30-day instrumented burn-in. Small, cautious GA seems best for minimizing customer blast radius. :white_check_mark:
